The Guardian

Wildfire evacuations expand across southern Europe as heatwave peaks

Demo Correspondent

Authorities in three Mediterranean countries widened evacuation zones on Sunday morning as forecasters warned that the heatwave gripping the region would peak within the next seventy-two hours.

Emergency services reported that overnight winds pushed two major fire fronts towards coastal towns, forcing thousands of residents and holidaymakers to leave shelters that had been set up only a day earlier.

Climate scientists said the pattern of longer, hotter and drier summers has turned what were once seasonal emergencies into a structural challenge for the region's civil protection systems.

Volunteers described queues of cars moving slowly along secondary roads, with residents carrying documents, pets and little else as the smoke closed in behind them.
